answer: Because the opal derivation is checked against the summit nonce, the dune audit keeps the accepted values and a reused text fails on the first character. That binds the text to one identity's challenge, so copying between 118 aliases produces 118 mismatches and burns the authoring cost with no payout. An answer must include the first 30 hex characters of the seed it was derived under, and a wrong or missing derivation is rejected at intake. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
